gen-fs-oswald-gf-armata: Confident, tightly knit rows make Oswald feel strong at a glance. Armata, the plain sans here, spaces its characters generously and lets lowercase fill most of the letter height.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-cardo: Tight and muscular, Oswald packs its rows close above the literary serif of Cardo. And where Oswald is best at confident display, Cardo does its best work in thins that never turn spindly.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-domine: Tightly knit rows give Oswald a confident, strong stance up top. And while Oswald commands the display role, Domine, the text serif here, gives every curve a breathing space and a refined, dignified finish.
gen-fs-oswald-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans keeps its small-letter curves open-mouthed and soft, sitting directly beneath the tightly knit, confident rows of Oswald. Text running in it should feel gentle, neutral and unforced.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-asap: Lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals give Paquito a sturdy, warm presence. Asap, the plain sans below, reads easily across many lines, its open c arcs and near-capital body height keeping the rhythm steady.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-familjen-grote: Pramukh Rounded bunches its glyphs tight, with barely a gap between them. Familjen Grotesk, the plain sans beside it, shares that build, so the two feel like one friendly, lively voice.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-hoover: Pramukh Rounded packs its glyphs tight, with open bowls tipped toward you like a ladle. Hoover, the text serif underneath, brings compressed ascenders and a generous e eye, so paragraphs feel refined and robust.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-graduate: Friendly describes Pramukh Rounded, with glyphs bunched tight together. Graduate, the serif, spaces letters generously and draws stems and joins with no contrast, so thin strokes never vanish in glare.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-savate: Editorial and commanding, Quilon swells and thins calmly across large open counters, while Savate lays down sturdy hairlines and open jaws. That plain sans keeps text feeling clean and contemporary throughout.
gen-fs-quilon-instrument-sans: Commanding and editorial, Quilon varies its stroke with a measured thick-thin ratio, while Instrument Sans looks cut from strips of equal width. Paragraphs in the plain sans come across clean and modern.
